cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
Addendum to existing finding #38: beyond the already documented NYSED shortener artifact, this supplies verified encoding/response contrasts, all six requested aggregate selections and an exact later archive readback. This strengthens outcome evidence while leaving requester and AI attribution unresolved.

On May 17, 2026, an NYSED enrollment query for Brookfield CSD has six archive captures with the literal query value x=/, all HTTP 403, and six otherwise matching captures with x=%2F, all HTTP 200. The earliest pair is 02:45:56 and 02:47:10 UTC. Four representative enrollment/homepage bodies were independently verified; the successful enrollment page contains 2016-17 public aggregates: 219 K-12 pupils, with 110 under the male filter. A homepage pair repeats the rejection/success pattern, and later captures interleave. This encoding change is in a query parameter, not the URL path.

Separately, seven Ghostarchive records on May 17 preserve converter-delivered enrollment results for six year/ethnicity selections, all male: 2017 White 105/219 and Black 1/219; 2018 White 103/222 and Black 1/222; 2019 White 98/214 and Black 0/214. The year labels denote school years ending in those years. On May 18 at 08:52:46 UTC, archive RXLQV records a converter request naming the exact earlier qaSYK WARC and returns 19,072 bytes including its context and 105/219 figures. This is a specific later retrieval of a prior saved output, not merely another similar target URL.

These observations support a practical encoding-related retrieval workaround, actual public aggregate delivery and archive-output reuse. Missing original sessions/headers prevent isolating the encoding as the sole cause or identifying the historical rejecting component. Converter records do not independently reveal every backend origin transaction or exclude caching. Published traversal, altered-extension, null-byte and semicolon variants are separate intent evidence; their historical execution and success have not been established. No individual student records or authentication bypass is shown.

No authenticated operator, common author, AI reader or provider is identified. Untapped source is No for this bounded response/readback finding; unresolved execution of published variants is an evidence gap rather than a newly identified substantial corpus.
data.summary: NYSED records show a repeated query-encoding/rejection contrast, delivery of public enrollment selections and later readback of an exact archive. Separate traversal/null-byte links have no established execution.
